summary: Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. In 1884, he was Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and permanently at Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shrikant S. Bahulkar is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held posts at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak (~1898–1904). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1904–1927), honorary secretary at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1917–1942), and General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference (~1919–1943).

Shrivatsa Goswami is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University, where he also taught. He founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana in 1972 and held posts at Harvard's Center for the Study of World Religions and Vrindaban Research Institute.

Shu-Fen Chen works in linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock, later holding a professorship at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shu-chen Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned a PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen C. Lang, as well as Bradley W. Reed and Ronald G. Dimberg, and served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held a professorship at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata, earning a BA and doctorate, and taught at Komazawa from assistant (1971) to professor (1984, 2014). He also served as acting head of Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. After studying in Lyon and Paris, he taught at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and National Academy of Art, and served as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato was a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo and University of Paris, he held teaching posts at Tokyo, Sophia, British Columbia, Berlin, Munich, and Ritsumeikan, directing the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.
Shuichi Maida was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University and studied under Haya Akegarasu around 1930.

Shuichi Nara is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University. He held positions as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University (attested 2026).

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (2003) and researcher at Bukkyo University (2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2006), and Musashino University (2006).
Shujiro Shimada was a scholar of Japanology, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1928 to 1931 and later held a post at Princeton University from ~1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and at Kyoto University, later serving as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University.

Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He spent his career at Komazawa University rising from research assistant (1973) to professor (1991), and was a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1998).
Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi and earned a PhD from Northwestern University under the supervision of Brook Ziporyn.

Shuming Liang was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who attended Shuntian Middle School. He joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and founded both the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and the China Democratic League.

Shumpei Ueyama was a philosophy and Japanology scholar educated at Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University from 1954, becoming professor in 1968 and emeritus professor in 1982, and served as Director of Kyoto National Museum and President of Kyoto City University of Arts.
Shun Hidaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).
